cards.explanation: The answer is a heap of ruins. The LORD says, “Behold, Damascus is no longer a city; it has become a heap of ruins.” (Isaiah 17:1) That's not a city with a few cracks in the wall, friends. I've seen a cookie sheet hit the floor with more left standing than that.

The answer is flocks. The cities of Aroer are forsaken, and the verse says they “…will be left to the flocks, which will lie down with no one to fear.” (Isaiah 17:2) Think about that for a second, friends. The new tenants are animals, and they're about the most relaxed neighbors a street ever had.

The answer is the Israelites. The LORD of Hosts declares, “The remnant of Aram will be like the splendor of the Israelites…” (Isaiah 17:3). I'm not going to guess what that comparison means, friends, because the verse doesn't spell it out. I'll just point at what it says and keep my mustache still.

The answer is fade. The LORD says, “In that day the splendor of Jacob will fade…” (Isaiah 17:4). Think of my apron after way too many washes, friends. The splendor was there, and then it starts to go.

The answer is True! The LORD says, “Yet gleanings will remain…” (Isaiah 17:6). The reaper has been through, but something is still left behind. Even after a hard sweep, the text points to what remains.

The answer is Maker. “In that day men will look to their Maker and turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel.” (Isaiah 17:7) After all that ruin, the eyes finally go up. The very next verse says they will not look to the altars they have fashioned with their hands. I love when somebody looks at the right One, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, “They will not look to the altars they have fashioned with their hands…” (Isaiah 17:8). They turned their eyes to their Maker in the verse before. Once you're looking up, friends, you're not staring at your own handiwork.

The answer is forgotten. “For you have forgotten the God of your salvation…” (Isaiah 17:10). The next part says they also failed to remember the Rock of their refuge. Forgetting is easy, friends. I've forgotten where I put my own mixing spoon, but this is a much bigger thing to lose track of.

The answer is that it will vanish. “…yet the harvest will vanish on the day of disease and incurable pain.” (Isaiah 17:11) The verses before it say they cultivate delightful plots and set out cuttings from exotic vines. All that planting and tending, and then it's gone. That's about the saddest empty tray I can picture, friends.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, “He rebukes them, and they flee far away…” (Isaiah 17:13). All that rumbling like mighty waters, and when the rebuke comes, they run. Nobody is planting their feet in that verse.

The answer is before morning! “In the evening, there is sudden terror! Before morning, they are no more!” (Isaiah 17:14) Sudden terror comes in the evening, and before morning, they're gone. That's all inside one night, friends.

The answer is True. The message says, “This is the portion of those who loot us and the lot of those who plunder us.” (Isaiah 17:14) That's how the passage ends, friends, with a clear word about what happens to them. Short, sharp, and nothing added.
